Last week, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing a former employee of stealing trade secrets "for OpenAI's benefit."

It's reported that during the lawsuit proceedings, Apple directly contacted several former employees who currently work at OpenAI.

According to the Financial Times, Apple has issued evidence preservation letters to approximately 40 former employees.

An evidence preservation letter is a formal written notice sent to an individual or organization requiring them to preserve documents, records, and other evidence related to a legal dispute. Such letters typically specify what needs to be preserved.

This move stems from Apple's suspicion that the trade secret theft may extend beyond the individuals named in last week's initial lawsuit.

In short, Apple's lawsuit names OpenAI and io Products, as well as former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan, as defendants.

You can read more details about Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI:

  • Apple sues OpenAI, alleging former employee stole trade secrets
  • An email mishap derailed pre-lawsuit negotiations between Apple and OpenAI
  • Apple's complaint documents reveal how many former employees currently work at OpenAI
  • OpenAI says it has seen no evidence to support Apple's trade secret theft allegations
  • Apple's lawsuit has not affected OpenAI's hardware release timeline

You can read the full copy of Apple's initial complaint documents here.
